species: rat (ZDF, DIO/STZ, lean Zucker Sprague-Dawley), mouse (western-diet obesity), swine (healthy); rat dorsal root ganglion neurons (in vitro)
condition_other: type-2 diabetes / diet-induced obesity / insulin resistance rodent models (ZDF, DIO, western-diet); healthy swine used for euglycaemic clamp studies
readout_other: Blood glucose/insulin/HOMA-IR, circulating hormone panels (leptin, GLP-1, ghrelin, catecholamines), hypothalamic PVN single-unit firing (glucose-excited/inhibited neurons), cFOS/BDNF/GLUT4 immunohistochemistry, RNA-seq and untargeted metabolomics of multiple tissues, calcium imaging (Fluo4) in 3D DRG neuron cultures
direction_notes: pFUS at the porta hepatis activated afferent liver-brain nerve pathways (increased hypothalamic catecholamines, IRS-1, GLUT4, DRG calcium transients) and lowered blood glucose/improved insulin sensitivity across species, but effects on individual circulating hormones (leptin, GLP-1, ghrelin, norepinephrine) and on hypothalamic glucose-excited vs glucose-inhibited neuron firing differed in direction between models/neuron types, and the effect was abolished by nerve transection, chemical nerve block or TRPA1 channel blockade.
safety_notes: No adverse pFUS-induced deviations of serum biomarkers were observed; circulating glucose, T4, cholesterol and amylase stayed in the normal range compared with sham controls, and the stimulation parameters used in the swine studies were kept within current FDA diagnostic-ultrasound limits (<720 mW/cm2 Ispta.3 and <1.9 MI).

exposures.label: Chronic/acute hepatic pFUS in ZDF/DIO rats and western-diet mice (1.1 MHz pre-clinical system)

target.label: hepatoportal nerve plexus at the porta hepatis

timing.protocol_description: pFUS was applied transcutaneously to the image-marked porta hepatis under isoflurane anaesthesia for 3 min, once daily for chronic studies (up to 40-56 d) or as a single stimulus before an oral/IV glucose tolerance test; sham animals underwent identical handling with the transducer powered off. One description of the ZDF-pFUS protocol states '150 burst cycles, 500 microsecond burst period', which would imply either a ~136 microsecond pulse (consistent with the 150 microsecond nominal pulse duration) at an unstated repetition period, or a much higher (2 kHz) repetition rate than the '5 Hz pulse repetition frequency' given as the nominal system setting; this could not be resolved.

exposures.label: Hepatic pFUS during hypothalamic (PVN) electrophysiological recording (2.5 MHz system)

target.label: hepatoportal nerve plexus at the porta hepatis (during PVN single-unit recording)

device.model: custom-made 2.5 MHz focused single-element ultrasound transducer

timing.protocol_description: Used only for the hypothalamic PVN single-unit recording experiments (Fig. 5), where hepatic pFUS was delivered while glucose-sensing PVN neuron firing was recorded following intraperitoneal glucose injection; stimulation duration for this specific protocol is not stated.

exposures.label: Hepatic pFUS in swine during hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (clinical GE LOGIQ E10 system)

target.label: hepatoportal nerve plexus at the porta hepatis (swine)

device.model: LOGIQ E10 with C1-6 abdominal probe

timing.protocol_description: In healthy swine, a 3 min pFUS stimulus was applied to the ultrasound-image-targeted porta hepatis during a hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp, using a clinically available diagnostic ultrasound system reconfigured in research mode; parameters were designed to achieve a mechanical index of ~1.77, within current FDA diagnostic-ultrasound limits.

exposures.label: In vitro pFUS stimulation of 3D dorsal root ganglion neuron cultures

target.label: primary dorsal root ganglion (DRG) sensory neurons in 3D hydrogel culture

device.model: H102 single-element focused transducer (pre-clinical hepatic pFUS system)

timing.protocol_description: 3D cultures of DRG sensory neurons in porous hydrogel scaffolds were stimulated with the same pre-clinical hepatic pFUS transducer/generator system, coupled to each culture well, using pulse parameters and pressures corresponding to the in vivo hepatic experiments; calcium (Fluo4) imaging showed increased fluorescence during pFUS 'on' periods that returned to baseline when pFUS was turned off, and this response was blocked by mechanosensitive/TRPA1 channel blockers (GsMTx4, HC-030031) but not by TTX or omega-conotoxin.

flags.reason: This is a multi-species, multi-experiment paper (chronic/acute glucose studies, clamps, nerve-block studies, electrophysiology, multi-omics, in vitro) with dozens of small, non-overlapping cohorts (n typically 4-20) and no single stated aggregate subject total; left not_reported.

One sentence describing the ZDF-pFUS protocol gives '150 burst cycles, 500 microsecond burst period', which is hard to reconcile with the system's stated nominal '150 microsecond pulse duration' and '5 Hz pulse repetition frequency'; not entered as a numeric value because the intended quantities are unclear.

Two different derated Ispta values are reported for the same 1.1 MHz rodent system: 94.3 +/- 11.2 mW/cm2 from bench characterisation at the nominal 135 mV drive amplitude, and ~581 mW/cm2 'at the ~5 mm target depth in the rats' quoted when describing the swine dose; both are retained as list entries since the paper does not reconcile them (likely different drive amplitudes, given the stated linear MI-vs-amplitude scaling).
The stimulus duration used during the PVN electrophysiology recording experiments (Fig. 5) is not stated; the 3-min duration used elsewhere is not assumed to apply.

The in vitro DRG culture experiments reuse the pre-clinical 1.1 MHz hepatic pFUS system, but no pulse duration, PRF, duty cycle or per-trial duration specific to the culture experiments is stated in the text; only the 0.83 MPa peak-positive pressure is given.

Effects on circulating hormones (leptin, GLP-1, ghrelin, norepinephrine) differed in direction between the ZDF and DIO models, and pFUS attenuated but did not reverse the direction of glucose-induced firing-rate changes in hypothalamic glucose-excited neurons; classified as mixed_or_unclear rather than a single direction.
